subject.title: fix(acp): keep completed run-mode sessions resumable

question: Should OpenClaw retain confirmed-resumable completed one-shot metadata as the supported ACP lifecycle contract, including backend pinning and fail-closed missing-target behavior?
rationale: This fixes a reproduced bug but intentionally changes persisted session cleanup and dependency-facing resume semantics, which require ACP owner intent rather than automated repair judgment.

options.title: Accept gated retention
options.body: Approve the capability-, identity-, readiness-, and backend-gated lifecycle and land after exact-head checks and dependency review pass.

options.title: Require upstream ACPX surface
options.body: Pause landing until reusable capability detection or resume-error normalization is exposed by ACPX and the OpenClaw wrapper is narrowed.

options.title: Preserve terminal closure
options.body: Keep one-shot metadata terminally closed and reject post-completion follow-ups, leaving continued conversation to persistent ACP sessions.

recommendation.title: Accept gated retention
recommendation.body: Approve the capability-, identity-, readiness-, and backend-gated lifecycle and land after exact-head checks and dependency review pass.

likelyOwner.reason: Their ACPX process, routing, and session-lifecycle history most directly spans the compatibility boundary under review.
